title: Qualify the candidate and establish the 1.0 freeze
goal: Demonstrate a stable API/SPI/schema on one candidate commit in real consumers and make the release gate and post-1.0 compatibility comparison blocking.
context: Architecture phase D (revision 2, D4, D6, D9, D12). Approximate size: M. The candidate closes the one pre-1.0 transition; only fixes demonstrated necessary by qualification are allowed. Physical extraction remains conditional future work.

consumes: The relocated implementation and evidence from P1–P3
produces: Stable-tag comparison in CI (I18) with the chosen structural comparison tool or generator diff
Recorded race and load evidence against prior profiles (I22)
Complete upgrade guide and release notes
boundaries: 1.0 requires every release condition on the candidate commit
A tag cannot bypass the candidate qualification matrix
A PR cannot replace the compatibility baseline silently
Future relocation keeps FQCNs, formats, migration basenames and data

include: API generator, ApiManifestTest and tests/Arch rules in blocking mode
Driver/cache/replica, race, load and consumer suites

pitfalls: Regenerating a manifest on the same branch does not prove compatibility
continue-on-error checks do not qualify a distribution
Release validation on a tag must cover the qualified candidate
Interface additions, named parameters, defaults and closed-enum cases can break implementers

validation.procedure: Verify the ten release conditions on the candidate commit with the evidence named in knowledge/architecture#release-gate, and prove that the stable-tag comparison and tag gating fail on intentional breaking fixtures (interface method, parameter rename, closed-enum case, payload key, migration basename).
validation.expect: Every condition green with reproducible evidence; every intentional break is rejected.

deliverables: Frozen API/SPI, schema and machine-format baselines

sections.title: Mandatory design inputs
sections.text:
The detailing session for P4 reads these before authoring any item (`show` of this phase is the entry point; the list is mandatory):

```bash
P='python3 <task>/scripts/plan.py'; ID=2026.10.10-№1-AZGUARD-CORE-STABILIZATION
$P get $ID knowledge/architecture --section release-gate
$P get $ID knowledge/architecture --section invariants
$P get $ID knowledge/architecture --section api-compatibility
$P get $ID knowledge/architecture --section transition-policy
$P get $ID knowledge/architecture --section risks
$P get $ID knowledge/contracts            # all sections
$P get $ID knowledge/identities            # all sections
$P get $ID knowledge/upgrade-map            # all sections (becomes UPGRADING.md)
$P get $ID knowledge/type-map            # rules
$P get $ID D4
$P get $ID D6
$P get $ID D9
$P get $ID D12
$P get $ID D13
```

Rules for the detailed items:

- Each item lists in `reads` (with `section`, `required: true`) the reference sections it implements; a phase-bound document that no item reads is reported by `design-done` (`phase_documents_unread`) and must be resolved before the phase counts as detailed.
- Items cite their type-map rows by current FQCN in `scope.include`; an item may not move, rename or re-mark a type differently from `knowledge/type-map`.
- If `design-done` reports a pack over the 256 KB budget, move the binding of a reference document from the phase to the items that read it (`plan.py unlink … --kind applies_to`, `plan.py link …`) — never drop the read.
- Baselines are taken from the candidate; the intentional-break fixtures cover one example per frozen category of `knowledge/identities` and `knowledge/contracts`.

sections.title: Exit criterion
sections.text: The documented 1.0 release gate is satisfied on one candidate commit with linked evidence, and no architecture boundary, contract or format remains undecided.
